tracks.narration: What if a flip-flop had just one rule — flip on every tick?
Here's a T flip-flop. T on top — the toggle enable. Clock on the bottom with the edge-trigger triangle. Q on the output side.
The truth table has two rows. With T at zero, Q stays put. With T at one, Q becomes the inverse of its previous value on every clock edge.
Watch what happens with T held high. Every time the clock ticks up, Q flips. The output frequency is exactly half the clock — one T flip-flop is a divide-by-two.
Stack three T flip-flops with each one's Q driving the next one's clock — the ripple counter. Eight binary states from three toggling bits.
